rows.question: Is the launch video building awareness of Zero among the people it reaches, and which creative does it better?
rows.kpi: Ad recall, aided awareness (primary); consideration, purchase intent (directional only)
rows.study: Brand lift survey on the video platform (randomized holdout)
rows.minimum: 3,418 test / 854 holdout answers per question; detects +4.3pp awareness, +3.2pp recall. Answers follow reach, not spend: half the budget (57M KRW) still detects +4.8pp; a 30% holdout would detect +3.7pp
rows.decision: Keep or shift creative weight between A and B; keep the flight weight
rows.owner: Measurement partner designs and reads it; the platform runs the polls; the agency fixes the holdout before launch

rows.question: Is awareness growing across the market, including people the platform never reached?
rows.study: Brand tracking survey by an independent research vendor (monthly waves)
rows.minimum: 1,000 adults per monthly wave; margin of error about +-2.8pp; a change between two waves must exceed 5.7pp to be read. No holdout: it shows the level, not what caused it
rows.decision: Brand health against competitors; sanity check on platform lift
rows.owner: Advertiser's research vendor; measurement partner aligns its question wording with the brand lift

rows.question: How many online purchases did the ads add, beyond what the pixel credits?
rows.kpi: Incremental online purchases and revenue; online iROAS
rows.minimum: 10% user holdout in the campaign regions; detects a 7.6% lift in online orders (online iROAS 0.21). Needs the brand's purchase events shared through the pixel (about 75% of orders match a user)
rows.decision: Online bidding targets; how far to trust pixel ROAS week to week
rows.owner: Measurement partner designs and reads it; advertiser shares purchase events through the pixel

rows.question: Do the ads pay back once convenience-store and supermarket sales are counted?
rows.study: Geo experiment: video off in matched regions, read from the retail sell-out panel and online sales
rows.minimum: 12 of 40 regions dark (29% of sales) for 6 weeks; detects a 3.2% drop in their sales, i.e. any total iROAS of 0.49 or more. Half the regions would detect 0.46 but put 176M KRW of launch sales at risk (vs 98M). If the advertiser will not go dark, a +50% heavy-up in the same regions reads the return on extra spend instead (detectable 0.99), with no sales at risk
rows.decision: Whether the launch weight pays back; budget for the second half
rows.owner: Measurement partner sizes the regions; agency holds video off there; advertiser shares the sell-out panel

rows.question: How should the second-half budget be split across video, search, social and retail media?
rows.study: Marketing mix model of total sales, calibrated with the geo test (conversion lift sees online only, so it checks the model rather than calibrating it)
rows.minimum: 78 weeks of history, the launch weeks and the geo test with its cooldown read
rows.owner: Advertiser analytics with the agency; measurement partner supplies the calibration

rows.question: Which platform-reported numbers can the team use for weekly optimisation, and with what correction?
rows.study: Cross-check of platform reports against the studies above
rows.decision: Correction factors for the weekly dashboard
rows.owner: Agency applies the corrections; measurement partner updates them after each study

rules: Primary metrics and holdout sizes are fixed before launch; no metric is promoted to primary after the results are in.
Creative A vs B is judged on ad recall and awareness only. Consideration and intent are too small to split by creative at this budget.

No early reads: brand lift is read after week 82, conversion lift and the geo test after week 88; the geo test is read again at week 90, two weeks after video returns, because launch awareness keeps selling.
If studies disagree, the study closest to the decision wins: the geo test for total payback, conversion lift for online bidding, brand lift for creative.

Success thresholds agreed in advance: awareness lift at least +3pp among people reached; for payback, the long-run sales return (MMM calibrated to the geo test) is compared with break-even at FIZLY's contribution margin, not with 1.0. Sales here are shelf value, so a return of 1.0 loses money.
